intro: The second subjective use of the modals reports claims rather than grading them. sollen = hearsay: Er soll sehr reich sein (people say he is); Das Restaurant soll ausgezeichnet sein; Sie soll den Unfall gesehen haben (is said to have seen). wollen = a claim the subject makes about themselves, which the speaker relays with a raised eyebrow: Sie will den Unfall gesehen haben (she claims she saw it); Er will von nichts gewusst haben (claims to have known nothing). Both take the same shape as the supposition modals: present infinitive for a present claim, Partizip II + haben / sein for a past one, and the passive too (Das Haus soll 2020 gebaut worden sein — is said to have been built). sollen is the journalist's tool for unconfirmed reports (Der Minister soll zurücktreten wollen — is reportedly planning to resign); wollen is the courtroom's (Der Angeklagte will zur Tatzeit zu Hause gewesen sein). Use both actively — and learn to hear the difference between 'soll' (others say) and 'will' (he says). This quiz is a transformation drill: each item gives you a report (Man sagt, … / Er behauptet, … / Angeblich …) and you compress it into soll or will plus the right infinitive — present, past (gewesen sein, gewusst haben) or passive past (gestohlen worden sein). The modals of supposition (muss, dürfte, könnte) have their own quiz.
tips[0].title: sollen = others say
tips[0].text: Er soll sehr reich sein. Das Medikament soll gut wirken. Der Chef soll die Firma verkaufen wollen (reportedly wants to). Past: Sie soll den Unfall gesehen haben. Er soll als Kind in Wien gelebt haben. = Man sagt / Es heißt / Angeblich …
tips[0].check.why: sollen reports what others say (= man sagt); muss would be your own conclusion, and a museum can't claim anything about itself.
tips[1].title: wollen = he says of himself (and I doubt it)
tips[1].text: Sie will den Unfall gesehen haben. Er will von nichts gewusst haben. Der Zeuge will den Täter erkannt haben. Niemand will etwas gehört haben. The subject makes the claim; wollen signals the speaker's distance.
tips[1].trap: 'Er will gewonnen haben' is not 'he wants to have won'. With a past infinitive, wollen almost always means 'claims'. Read the shape.
tips[1].check.why: wollen + past infinitive relays a claim the subject makes about himself, with the speaker's distance; soll would mean other people say so.
tips[2].title: Passive and modal inside the claim
tips[2].text: Das Haus soll 2020 gebaut worden sein (is said to have been built). Das Bild soll gestohlen worden sein. Der Minister soll zurücktreten wollen (reportedly wants to resign — two modals). Er will nicht gewarnt worden sein (claims not to have been warned).
tips[2].check.why: The past passive infinitive is Partizip II + worden + sein: gebaut worden sein. geworden is only for werden as a full verb ('become').
tips[2].visual.rows[0].a: Das Bild soll gestohlen worden sein.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].b: People say the picture was stolen.
tips[3].title: soll = Konjunktiv I compressed
tips[3].text: Man sagt, er sei reich = Er soll reich sein. The reported-speech Konjunktiv and subjective sollen do the same work; sollen is shorter and works without an introducing verb. Both belong to the journalist's toolbox.
tips[3].trap: Without a past infinitive, "Der Minister soll zurücktreten" is ambiguous and usually objective: someone demands that he resign. For the rumour, use the past infinitive (soll zurückgetreten sein) or soll … wollen (soll zurücktreten wollen).
tips[3].check.why: Es heißt + Konjunktiv I and subjective sollen both report hearsay; muss would be an inference and will a claim by the company itself.
remember[0]: soll = people say; will = he claims. Past: + Partizip II + haben/sein.
remember[1]: Passive inside: soll gebaut worden sein.
table.caption: Hearsay and self-claim
mistakes[2].why: The self-claim about the past uses the past infinitive.
mistakes[3].why: soll + present infinitive often reads as a demand; the rumour about a past event needs the past infinitive.
hook: Pass on rumours and doubtful claims like a journalist: er soll reich sein, sie will nichts gesehen haben.
recall.known: From "Subjektives sollen": er soll reich sein, er will … haben.
recall.today: Passive and modal inside the claim: soll gestohlen worden sein.
